verdict.rationale: Ollama's own API docs give a stability and deprecation commitment: the API is expected to stay backwards compatible, and deprecations will be announced in the release notes. The same docs state the API isn't strictly versioned, so only the deprecation-policy half of the story is delivered, and only in a lightweight form. A published OpenAPI 3.1.0 spec adds some contract clarity. Missing for 10: formal API versioning (version paths or headers), a defined sunset/deprecation timeline, and independent corroboration that the stability commitment holds in practice.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can rely on versioned APIs with a documented deprecation policy

citations.quote: Ollama's API isn't strictly versioned, but the API is expected to be stable and backwards compatible. Deprecations are rare and will be announced in the release notes.
